key_insight: Detonation-sprayed self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings can be tuned from low-friction to high-wear-resistance behavior by adjusting barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical parameter map for optimizing surface restoration and strengthening of machine parts using detonation spraying.
method: Adjusted working-gas molar ratio (O/C = 1.026–1.856) and inter-shot delay (0–1 s).
Compared coating microstructure, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear response.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed the lowest friction at 48% filling and O/C = 1.026, while the best wear resistance occurred at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s delay, reducing specific wear rate to 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Lower-friction settings increased wear, so the operating point must be chosen as a trade-off rather than a single-parameter optimum.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
